userStories.title: Calibrate the PR reviewer and parse finding origins
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Give every bot PR reviewer the exact severity scale and grounded normal definition, solicit origin only when in-range pushes are actually listed, and parse optional origin metadata.

**Motivation** — The bot PR review prompt has no severity scale.

**Approach** — The reply schema gains `origin` and `originEvidence` per finding, asked only when the prompt lists in-range bot pushes (US-002). The prompt text is facts, not orders. It defines the classes and asks for them, as the trigger classes already are. It says nothing about what a class or a severity does to readiness, and nothing about how to fix.

A reply may state an origin on a review that was not asked for one: a full review, or one whose prompt lists no bot push. The parser keeps it, and `settleFindingOrigins` checks it exactly as it checks an asked one. A `fix-gap` claim then stands only on a line lineage attributes to a bot push, which is the same fact an asked claim needs. Settlement is implemented by US-003, not by this parser.

`PrFinding` (`packages/nax/src/operations/bot-types.ts`). Target: gains `readonly origin?: FindingOrigin;` and `readonly originEvidence?: string;`. Absent origin means `pr`.

`findings()` (`packages/nax/src/operations/bot-pr-review-reply.ts`). Target: also sets `origin` to `parseFindingOrigin(source.origin)` only when that returns a value, and `originEvidence` to the same trimmed, 300-character-capped form `triggerEvidence` uses, only when non-empty. A finding with no known origin carries neither field. Keep the existing trigger parsing and optional triggerEvidence unchanged. `MAX_TRIGGER_EVIDENCE_CHARS = 300` and `triggerEvidence(value)` (a non-empty trimmed string capped at 300, else `undefined`) already exist.

`TASK_CONTRACT` and `replyTask` (`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/bot-pr-review-builder.ts`). Target: the contract is composed per prompt. These lines are added or changed. Every other line of the contract keeps its exact text and order.
- After the line `Set "decision" on a finding only when it breaks a listed project decision. The "decision" field is optional.` comes the new line `Severity: "critical" = unsafe behaviour or lost data a user or caller can reach; "important" = other wrong behaviour a user or caller can reach, a changed behaviour no test would catch, or a break of a listed project rule; "minor" = worth noting.` It is in every contract, conversation-only included.
- The `normal` definition line becomes `normal: reachable in ordinary use of the product, as this repository documents or configures it.`
- The doc comment on `replyTask`, which says a conversation-only task is byte-for-byte the text from before the approval line existed, is reworded: that task now also carries the `Severity:` line and the new `normal` definition.
- When `pushSection(input)` renders, the four lines below follow the `manual:` definition line, and the finding shape in the JSON example gains `, "origin": "pr|fix-regression|fix-gap", "originEvidence": "..."` directly after `"triggerEvidence": "..."`. When it does not render, neither appears.

```text
Name each finding's origin with "origin" and the one detail that shows it with "originEvidence". The origins are:
pr: the problem is in the pull request's own change.
fix-regression: a push listed under "Earlier nax bot fix pushes in this range" broke behaviour that worked before that push.
fix-gap: a further gap in code a push listed under "Earlier nax bot fix pushes in this range" added to close an earlier item, where the behaviour before that push was the same or worse.
```

`packages/nax/src/prompts/builders/bot-pr-review-builder.ts`: `pushSection(input)` renders `## Earlier nax bot fix pushes in this range` only when `input.incrementalSince !== undefined`, `input.conversationOnly` is not true, and `input.botPushes` yields at least one line. Unchanged. Use the actual rendered-section condition, not just a nonempty entry array. A full/first review, conversation-only review or incremental review with no rendered push section is not asked for origin, even though a reply volunteering it is accepted.

**Scope** — In: bot-specific finding types, context-free reply parsing, composed bot PR review contract and prompt/parser tests. `packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder.test.ts` — the `taskContract` constant pins the whole contract text verbatim, and `preChangeTask` and `taskWithApprovalLine` are built from it (used by the tests at lines 218, 488 and 494). It gains the `Severity:` line after the `Set "decision"` line, and its `normal:` line becomes `normal: reachable in ordinary use of the product, as this repository documents or configures it.` Those prompts list no bot push, so no origin line is added. The AC-9 `test.each` row for `normal` changes to the same new definition. Every other row and assertion stays. Add severity cases to that file and parser cases to packages/nax/test/unit/operations/bot-pr-review-reply.test.ts. Create packages/nax/test/unit/prompts/bot-pr-review-builder-origin.test.ts for AC-5 through AC-10 because its existing sibling is 578 lines. Out: US-001 owns shared vocabulary/blocking/rendering; US-003 owns deterministic settlement/posting/artifacts; US-004 owns earlier carry/readiness. Do not change workflow-quality-checklist.ts, other reviewers' severity scales, the review/fix model, or add readiness/fix instructions to the prompt.

**Interface**
```typescript
// PrFinding gains:
readonly origin?: FindingOrigin;
readonly originEvidence?: string;
```
The reply accepts `"origin": "pr|fix-regression|fix-gap"` and `"originEvidence": "..."` without requiring prompt context. Unknown or absent origin is represented by omitted fields, not a materialized pr value.

userStories.title: Settle fix-gap claims before recording or posting reviews
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Back every fix-gap claim with existing line lineage and absence of an own inline thread before recording or publishing the review, preserving origin into agreed artifacts and fix eligibility.

**Motivation** — Nothing in the blocking decision used the facts, so a finding in code a fix had just added blocked like a finding in the original change.

**Approach** — `settleFindingOrigins` checks each `fix-gap` claim against the lineage, and against the bot's own inline threads, before anything is posted or recorded (US-003). A reply may state an origin on a review that was not asked for one: a full review, or one whose prompt lists no bot push. The parser keeps it, and `settleFindingOrigins` checks it exactly as it checks an asked one. A `fix-gap` claim then stands only on a line lineage attributes to a bot push, which is the same fact an asked claim needs.

A `fix-gap` claim also never stands on a finding the bot already posted as an inline thread. A `fix-gap` finding gets no thread, so an own thread for the key means the finding was posted while it blocked. Re-raising it, even with unchanged wording on a line a later fix touched, keeps it blocking until it is fixed or ruled on. Without this, an unfixed original blocker could pass the lineage check on its own re-raise.

`settleFindingOrigins` (new, `packages/nax/src/bot/finding-origin.ts`). Target: `export function settleFindingOrigins(verdict: PrReviewVerdict, facts: { readonly lineage: PostReviewInput["lineage"]; readonly ownThreadKeys: ReadonlySet<string> }): PrReviewVerdict`. It returns a new verdict and never mutates its input. For each finding whose `origin` is `"fix-gap"`, with `key = findingKey(finding)`: when `facts.lineage?.lineage.has(key)` and `!facts.ownThreadKeys.has(key)`, the finding is unchanged. Otherwise the finding's `origin` becomes `"pr"`, its `originEvidence` is dropped, and one `debug` log line names the key. Findings with any other origin, or none, are unchanged.

`postPrReview` builds `ownThreadKeys` from `input.own`: the `key` of every entry whose `threadId` is defined. A top-level own comment (summary, carried record, signals) has no `threadId` and is not counted.

`postPrReview` (same file). Target: its first statement replaces the input's verdict with `settleFindingOrigins(input.verdict, { lineage: input.lineage, ownThreadKeys })`, and every later call in the function reads the settled input. Build the inline-thread key set within this initial replacement so settlement precedes even reviewId creation/persistence. Replace the local input with an immutable copy rather than modifying caller data. The supplied code currently creates reviewId before persistArtifact; leave that generation after settlement.

`AgreedItem` finding variant and `agreedItems` (`packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts`). Target: the variant gains `readonly origin?: FindingOrigin;` and `readonly originEvidence?: string;`. `agreedItems` copies both from the verdict finding when present, like `trigger` and `triggerEvidence`.

`post.ts` is 563 lines against the 600-line source limit, so `settleFindingOrigins` lives in its own file and `post.ts` gains only the calls and the copied fields. Use a type-only import for PostReviewInput in the new module to avoid a runtime import cycle.

Integration facts to reuse, not change: `packages/nax/src/bot/lineage.ts`: `computeLineage(input, deps): Promise<LineageResult>`, `LineageResult { lineage: ReadonlyMap<string, FindingLineage>; unknown: ReadonlySet<string>; unreachable: number }`. A key is in `lineage` only when a reachable recorded push wrote that finding's anchor line, so every entry has `generation >= 1`. A key whose blame or ancestry read failed is in `unknown` instead. A finding with no `file` or `line` is in neither. `packages/nax/src/bot/push-ledger.ts`: `FindingLineage { generation; parents; pushSha }`, `BotPushEntry`. `packages/nax/src/bot/render.ts`: `findingKey({ file, issue })`, the key both the lineage map and `agreedItems` use. `packages/nax/src/bot/review-run.ts`: the `post` node of `BOT_REVIEW_GRAPH` computes `lineage = await reviewLineage(env.post, state.verdict)` and then calls `_botReviewDeps.postPrReview({ ...env.post, verdict, ...(lineage === undefined ? {} : { lineage }) })`. Unchanged. `packages/nax/src/bot/review-blocking.ts`: `hasPushWorthyItem(env: BotFixEnv): boolean`, which asks `isBlockingFinding` of each agreed `finding` item. Unchanged.

`bot-review.json` is read back without a field whitelist (`fix-input.ts`), so `origin` survives into `hasPushWorthyItem` and readiness. A `fix-gap` item that reaches a fix session alongside push-worthy work gets the existing not-blocking fact line. Do not add origin prompt text for the fixer.

Failure handling: A `fix-gap` claim on a finding with no `file` or `line`, whose lineage read failed (key in `unknown`), on a line no reachable bot push wrote, or with lineage undefined because the PR has no push ledger reads `pr`. A `fix-regression` claim with no lineage (a fix that deleted a guard leaves no blamed line) is kept as `fix-regression`. It blocks either way. Settlement does not depend on whether the prompt asked for an origin.

**Scope** — In: new settlement module and its unit tests, settle-first post entry, artifact metadata copies and runBotReview posting/artifact tests, plus hasPushWorthyItem cases. Add integration ACs to packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-lineage.test.ts using its existing stubGit and summaryComment scaffolding; AC-15 adds one ancestry answer to stubGit (the blamed commit is not reachable from the push). No existing assertion in the file changes. Add AC-17 and AC-18 to packages/nax/test/unit/bot/review-blocking.test.ts with makeBotFixEnv from packages/nax/test/helpers/bot-fix.ts. Existing postPrReview callers pass verdicts with no origin, which settleFindingOrigins returns unchanged. agreedItems adds fields only when an origin is present, so every existing artifact and summary assertion stays. Out: US-001 owns shared blocking/rendering; US-002 owns prompt/parser; US-004 owns mergeEarlier/withoutFactLines, re-raise posting edge cases, minors and readyStep integration. Do not change computeLineage, review-run.ts's caller, push ledgers, artifact versions or deterministic checks for pr/fix-regression; no advisor routing, origin policy config or carried-record expansion.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function settleFindingOrigins(verdict: PrReviewVerdict, facts: { readonly lineage: PostReviewInput["lineage"]; readonly ownThreadKeys: ReadonlySet<string> }): PrReviewVerdict;
// AgreedItem finding variant gains:
readonly origin?: FindingOrigin;
readonly originEvidence?: string;
```

routing.reasoning: A deterministic map/set check in one new helper and a settle-first wrapper plus optional field copies in post.ts reuse existing lineage, posting and runBotReview fixtures; no new I/O or orchestration abstraction warrants heavier isolation.

userStories.title: Preserve earlier finding origins and readiness semantics
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry explicit origin facts from earlier own threads into agreed items without polluting issue text, and preserve the re-raise, minor and readiness outcomes through production entrypoints.

**Motivation** — Each round can then only remove blockers it agreed to, so the loop ends when the agreed work runs out, with no round cap and no human step.

**Approach** — `mergeEarlier` and `withoutFactLines` (`packages/nax/src/bot/post.ts`). Target: it also keeps `origin` when the thread body has a line starting `Origin:`, read with `readFindingThreadFacts(body).origin`, and `withoutFactLines` also drops lines starting `Origin:`. A body with no `Origin:` line carries no `origin` field. Preserve the existing trigger carry via earlierTrigger and continue dropping Trigger:/Lineage: metadata. Apply the common earlier-finding facts to both existing mergeEarlier branches.

A `fix-gap` claim also never stands on a finding the bot already posted as an inline thread. A `fix-gap` finding gets no thread, so an own thread for the key means the finding was posted while it blocked. Re-raising it, even with unchanged wording on a line a later fix touched, keeps it blocking until it is fixed or ruled on. Without this, an unfixed original blocker could pass the lineage check on its own re-raise.

Failure handling: A `fix-gap` claim on a finding whose key already has an own inline thread (posted earlier while it blocked, now re-raised) reads `pr`, so it still blocks. Its thread is edited in place as any blocking re-raise is, with no `Origin:` line, and it is not listed as residual. A `minor` `fix-gap` finding goes to `### Minor findings` as every minor does. That list renders no origin clause. A thread, summary or artifact written before this change has no `Origin:` line and no `origin` field: reads `pr`. An `Origin:` line with an unknown value reads `pr`.

A carried finding (`offLineFinding` in `post-carried.ts`) is built with no origin, so `### Still open from an earlier review` lines never show one. Keep this distinct from mergeEarlier: this story preserves an explicit fact on an earlier inline thread, not an origin field on the carried record.

Readiness is through the existing `readyStep` in packages/nax/src/bot/fix-report.ts and its private openFindingHold / blockingKeys, which already ask isBlockingFinding. `isBlockingFinding` applies three tests in this order, and a finding blocks only when it passes all three: severity is `critical` or `important`; origin is not `fix-gap` (an absent origin reads `pr`); trigger is in the effective blocking trigger set (an absent trigger reads `normal`). Do not add a second origin decision in readiness or bypass unrelated holds. US-003 supplies settlement; this story verifies that a lineage-backed re-raise still receives the own-thread veto before editing.

**Scope** — In: mergeEarlier explicit-origin carry, withoutFactLines cleanup, re-raise/minor/earlier-thread production posting scenarios, and readyStep hold/no-hold scenarios. The US-004 runBotReview ACs are added to packages/nax/test/integration/bot/review-run-lineage.test.ts, reusing stubGit, summaryComment and earlierThread. The `earlierThread(key, line, id)` helper hard-codes its opener body `**Important** (quality): Lock leaks`. It gains an optional fourth `body` parameter defaulting to that text, so the earlier-thread ACs can pass a body with fact lines. Every existing call and assertion stays as it is. The US-004 readyStep ACs go in packages/nax/test/unit/bot/fix-report.test.ts (425 lines), using the shared bot-fix helpers and _fixReportDeps rather than reimplementing readiness. Use no carried record and make all unrelated readiness inputs pass. Out: US-001 owns vocabulary/predicate/renderer changes; US-002 owns prompt/parser changes; US-003 owns settlement and initial artifact metadata copies. Do not expand carried v1 records or offLineFinding, alter chain-notice text, migrate historical records, change CI/head/settlement safeguards, add origin policy settings or route chains to an advisor.

**Interface** — The changed shared reader returns `{ severity: WorkflowSeverity; trigger: FindingTrigger; origin: FindingOrigin }`; mergeEarlier reads that origin only when the body explicitly contains an `Origin:` line. `AgreedItem`'s finding variant already has `readonly origin?: FindingOrigin;` and `readonly originEvidence?: string;` from US-003. Preserve only the origin required from the earlier thread; no new earlier-thread evidence parser or carried-record field is introduced.

outOfScope: Routing a fix-induced chain to the advisor for a design-level ruling (simplify, revert, fail closed, use a library), #2987 lever C. A later spec.
A config key (`bot.blockingOrigins`) or a per-PR writer ruling (`blocking origins: ...`) that changes which origins block. Build it only if real PRs show `fix-gap` findings that should have blocked.
Filing a follow-up issue that collects a PR's `fix-gap` residuals. The review summary's residual section is their only home.

Asking for an origin on a review whose prompt lists no in-range bot push: a full review, a first review, a conversation-only review, or an incremental review with no bot push in range. Such a review is not asked, so its findings normally carry no origin and read `pr`. An origin a reply states anyway is still checked against lineage.
A deterministic check of `fix-regression` or `pr` claims. Both block, so a wrong claim between them changes no readiness decision.
Showing a finding's origin to the bot fixer. The fixer already gets each finding's lineage (#2992 US-006), and a `fix-gap` finding alone causes no fix session (`hasPushWorthyItem`).
Changing the chain notice (`Findings are chasing their own fixes`). It lists blocking findings only, so a `fix-gap` finding leaves it, as a non-blocking trigger class already does.

Adding an origin field to the carried record (`<!-- nax-bot:carried v1 ... -->`) or to `offLineFinding`. The record holds only blocking findings. A `fix-gap` finding never blocks, and a carried `fix-regression` that reads `pr` still blocks, so no readiness decision changes.

The sentence `A state loss a caller can reach is a critical or important finding, never minor` in `workflow-quality-checklist.ts`. That checklist is shared with the workflow reviewers. The bot PR reviewer gets both texts: the checklist sets `important` as the floor for a reachable state loss, and the new scale names `critical` for lost data. The two agree that it is never `minor`, and both severities block, so the overlap changes no readiness decision.
